environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed in namespace 'logistics-prod' on a GKE cluster with Istio 1.19 service mesh (strict mTLS enforced cluster-wide via PeerAuthentication). An AuthorizationPolicy resource is applied to the inventory-service workload that uses a 'from' rule with source.namespaces set to ['logistics-prod'] combined with a 'when' condition requiring request.headers[x-correlation-trace] to be present. The orders-service (which would send bulk_allocate messages with attacker-controlled payloads) resides in namespace 'orders-prod'. The Istio sidecar proxy intercepts all inbound TCP connections to the inventory-service pod on port 3000 and port 5000 (gRPC). The AuthorizationPolicy action is DENY for sources NOT matching the specified namespace, effectively blocking cross-namespace traffic at L4 before it reaches the application container. Note: the policy uses a notNamespaces field under source rather than a positive allow-list, which means traffic from 'logistics-prod' namespace itself is permitted but the attacking orders-service cannot reach the vulnerable bulk_allocate endpoint.
